kurz: Dried mushrooms taste stronger than fresh ones: drying concentrates their umami, and the soaking water is almost as valuable as the mushrooms.
bild_im_kopf: Like a raisin plumping up again in rum: it soaks up the liquid, and the rum then tastes of raisin.
was_passiert: When drying, [[w-pilze|mushrooms]] lose almost all their water while the flavour compounds remain. Shiitake and porcini contain compounds that multiply the umami of [[glutamat|glutamate]]. In warm water the mushrooms soak up water again and release flavour into it.
warum_wichtig: A few dried mushrooms give [[g-risotto|risotto]], sauces and braises more depth than twice the amount of fresh ones.
faustregeln: Never pour away the soaking water: it is a ready-made mushroom stock.
Grind dried mushrooms to a powder and use it as seasoning on meat or in sauces.
schritte: Rinse the mushrooms briefly and put them in enough warm water to cover.
Soak for about 20 to 30 minutes until soft.
Lift out the mushrooms and squeeze them lightly.
Pour the water through a coffee filter so sand and grit stay behind.
Use both the mushrooms and the filtered water.
